sections.name: Tactical Gameplay Settings
sections.description:
The settings in this section alter the rules of the TACTICAL game, equally for enemies and mercs.
They have the potential to radically change the WAY THE GAME IS PLAYED, rather than simply changing the actual difficulty.

properties.name: NCTH
properties.description: Play with New Chance to Hit System (NCTH)?

properties.name: ALLOW_WALKING_WITH_WEAPON_RAISED
properties.description: Allow walking and sidesteps with raised weapons?

properties.name: ALLOW_ALTERNATIVE_WEAPON_HOLDING
properties.description:
This feature allows us to fire weapons in a different way: we can fire rifles (meaning any two handed guns) from hip, and pistols (meaning any one-handed guns) holding in hand (making standard pistol holding be with two hands). 
The benefit of such holding is speed (reduced AP cost to ready, faster target acquiring), the drawback is limited accuracy and no use of scopes. 
Here is the basic switch of the feature, it also controls how the feature behaves in game - the setting can go from 0-3, and here is explanation of each:
0 - Turned off entirely. 
1 - The alternative holding will be used only if you use NO aim clicks on a shots and you don't have your weapon raised up yet. 
2 - This behaviour allows several aim levels to be treated as "alternative weapon holding", based on total aiming levels 
    allowed for the gun. The number of alternative aim levels is always lesser than standard aim levels, and they are displayed
    as YELLOW dots under NCTH. If you do not have your gun raised yet (rifle to shoulder, pistol with two hands), you may fire
    from the alternative holding by simply aiming within the yellow aim levels limit (usually 33-66% of standard aim levels).
    If you use at least one aim click above the indicated alternative levels, your merc will automatically raise the weapon to 
    the standard holding before the shot.
3 - "Scope Mode" behaviour (default). This simply makes the alternative mode a "scope" mode. To fire rifle from hip or pistol
    one-handed, just press '.' key to cycle to the apropriate mode (currently indicated by an "eye" symbol). No matter if you
    have your rifle shouldered/pistol held two-handed, you will use the alternative mod anytime you select this mode. With this 
    setting, if you use the 'L' to raise your weapon, then it will be raised to a stance based on the scope mode selected.
    Of course, Scope Modes has to be allowed for this to work (they are as default).

Note that by now, this feature is only available in standing position (hopefully, in the future, I'll be able to finish 
animations for crouched stance). Also, by now it is unavailable for pistols when standing in water.
Last thing to mention: There is a new flag in Weapons.xml - "Heavygun" which says that weapon cannot be shouldered in standing position at all, and must be fired from hip then. It is only used for two-handed guns, supposedly for a rather too heavy LMGs.

properties.name: RAISE_TO_ALTWEAPHOLD_READY_APS_PERC
properties.description:
This says how many APs are charged to raise the weapon to alternative holdng (rifles to hip, pistols with one hand), based on standard weapon ready APs. Setting 25 here means 25% of the APs are charged to raise weapon to hip/one-handed, so a weapon with 12 APs to ready would charge 3 APs to raise to hip/one-handed. Default is 25% by now.
Note that this is also AP cost to go from shoulder to hip / from two-handed to one-handed grip.

properties.name: RAISE_FROM_ALTWEAPHOLD_READY_APS_PERCENTAGE
properties.description:
This determines how many APs from regular weapon ready APs are charged when going from alternative holding to standard holding.
This settings with the above one should put 100% together, as the alternative holding is supposed to be something like semi-raised gun (quarter-raised by now actullay).
This will not affect standard cost for raising weapons (when gun is lowered and we choose to raise it fully).

properties.name: FASTER_SHOT_FROM_ALTWEAPHOLD_PERC
properties.description: This makes the shots from alternative holding to cost less APs to make up for not being able to aim and use scopes. 10 here means -10% APs to shoot from hip / one-handed grip.

properties.name: CTH_PENALTY_FROM_ALTWEAPHOLD
properties.description: The base (N)CtH penalty when firing from alternative weapon holding.

properties.name: AIMING_PENALY_FROM_ALTWEAPHOLD
properties.description: The base penalty when aiming from alternative weapon holding, if aiming from it is allowed.

properties.name: AIMING_LEVELS_REDUCTION_ON_ALTWEAPHOLD
properties.description: Aiming levels of the gun are reduced percentually by this number on alternative weapon holding. So 50 here means only half aiming levels will be available when using alternative holding (keep in mind that is a positive thing in NCTH).

properties.name: WEAPON_RESTING
properties.description:
Should it be allowed to rest your weapon onto tables, rocks, open windows etc. if in crouched position? 
This basically gives you the boni you would get if in prone position, while you're in crouched position and behind a crate etc.

properties.name: WEAPON_RESTING_DISPLAY
properties.description:
Should a little 'M' indicate your weapon is currently rested against something (useful in the beginning, when your still 
unfamiliar with the feature)

properties.name: WEAPON_RESTING_PRONE_BONI_PERCENTAGE
properties.description:
Boni are calculated by this formula: WEAPON_RESTING_PRONE_BONI_PERCENTAGE * boni[PRONE] + (100 - WEAPON_RESTING_PRONE_BONI_PERCENTAGE) * boni[state you're in].
Value Range: 0 - 100.

properties.name: USE_SCOPE_MODES
properties.description:
Allow manual toggle between a gun's different scopes/sights (toggle via '.' in tactical).
Info: To see the difference field of views for the scopes, enable the mercenary-view by pressing SHIFT + V.

properties.name: DISPLAY_SCOPE_MODES
properties.description: Allow display of scope modes on weapons in tactical.

properties.name: SPOTTER_PREPARATIONTURNS
properties.description:
You can assign a merc to spot for fellow snipers via calling the Skill Menu (Shortcut: SHIFT+4) -> various -> Spotter.
You need an item the usSpotting-tag in your hands. 
The bonus applies to anyone of your team using a sniper weapon on a location your spotter can see.
Effectiveness depends on:
- spotters spotter item effectiveness (40%), experience (30%), marksmanship (20%) and leadership (10%)
- lowered by being wounded or fatigues
- altered by relation between spotter and sniper (base opinion, sexism, racism etc.) and spotter background

The bonus will be this many turns after activating the skill. Spending any AP with your spotter forfeits the bonus.

properties.name: SPOTTER_RANGE
properties.description:
This variable intentionally has two meanings. 
- A sniper will benefit from a spotter only if he is at maximum SPOTTER_RANGE tiles away from him. 
- The bonus only works on those locations the spotter can see and that are AT LEAST 2 * SPOTTER_RANGE tiles away.

properties.name: SPOTTER_MAX_CTHBOOST
properties.description: Maximum bonus that can be reached once spotter has waited 2 * SPOTTER_PREPARATIONTURNS turns

properties.name: EXTERNAL_FEEDING
properties.description:
Allow feeding a gun from external sources.
            0 = no eternal feeding
            1 = external feeding from the hands of other mercs
            2 = 1 + we can feed our own gun from dedicated slots from dedicated vests

properties.name: INITIAL_MERC_ARRIVAL_LOCATION
properties.description:
Set the grid number location where new hired merc arrive in the destination sector after you hired them.
            The JA2 default grid number is 4870.

properties.name: MAXIMUM_POSSIBLE_CTH
properties.description: Set the maximum possible "Chance to Hit" with any shot.

properties.name: MINIMUM_POSSIBLE_CTH
properties.description: Set the minimum possible "Chance to Hit" with any shot.

properties.name: MINIMUM_CTH_DIVISOR
properties.description:
Use this to set the minimum CTH of any shot to a value between 0 and 1. "MINIMUM_POSSIBLE_CTH" must be set to 0 for this to work.
            The minimum CTH is: 1 in every (x*100) bullets, where X is the value you set here.

properties.name: REALISTIC_TRACERS
properties.description:
Set the behaviour of the new Tracer Bullet system.
            0 = JA2 1.13 Default. Tracer magazines reduce the gun's auto/burst penalty. Every bullet in a Tracer magazine causes a lightpath.
            1 = Realistic Tracers. Only specific bullets in the magazine will show a lightpath, and they will "bump" the Chance-to-Hit up for all subsequent bullets in the same attack. Loading the tracer magazine into the gun does NOT reduce its burst/auto penalty.
            2 = Semi-Realistic Tracers. Same as option #1, but the tracer magazine also reduces the gun's auto/burst penalty.

properties.name: NUM_BULLETS_PER_TRACER
properties.description:
Determine the ratio between tracer bullets and normal bullets, in a Tracer Magazine. The ratio is 1 tracer to every X normals, where X is the value you set here.
            Requires REALISTIC_TRACERS to be set to 1 or 2.

properties.name: CTH_BUMP_PER_TRACER
properties.description: Set the "Chance-to-Hit" bonus that a tracer bullet bestows on ALL other bullets that follow it, in a single autofire volley.

properties.name: MIN_RANGE_FOR_TRACER
properties.description: Controls the minimum range at which tracers will improve our CTH.  Listed in Tiles.

properties.name: RANGE_EFFECT_ON_MAX_TRACER_CTH_BONUS
properties.description:
Determine the effect of range to target on calculating how high your CTH can go above its original value when using tracer ammo. Increase this value to make tracers less useful at long range. Decrease to make tracers more useful at long range.
            0 = Tracers can increase CTH indefinitely. The more you fire, the more accurate you are.
            3 = HAM Default. At a range of about 30 tiles, tracers can only increase your CTH back to its original value.
            See also REALISTIC_TRACERS.

properties.name: INCREASE_AIMING_COSTS
properties.description:
If set to TRUE, adding Extra Aiming to a single shot costs more APs than normal. The extra cost is based on the type of scope (if any) you are using, and the number of "aiming levels" you want to add.
            If set to FALSE, the game defaults to 4AP normal, 6AP with a Battle Scope (7x), and 8AP with a Sniper Scope (10x).
            Both can be completely toggled off using the in-game Options Menu. In that case, all aiming levels cost 4AP.

properties.name: ALLOW_EXTRA_AIM_LEVELS
properties.description: Basic setting to allow more than 4 aiming clicks for any gun

properties.name: FIRST_AIM_READY_COST_DIVISOR
properties.description:
When INCREASE_AIMING_COSTS = TRUE, this setting determines what fraction of your gun's "Ready Time" must be paid whenever you want to take an aimed shot. This setting is a divisor, so the amount of APs you must pay equals READY TIME / X, where X is the value you set here.
            0 = No extra aiming charge based on ready time.
            1 = Pay the full ready time for every aimed shot.
            2 = Pay half the ready time for every aimed shot.
            And so on. Please note: results are rounded down.
            The actual costs for each level are defined in APBPConstants.INI.

properties.name: AUTOFIRE_TOHIT_BONUS_MULTIPLIER
properties.description:
Converts the AutoFireToHitBonus of an item into a percentage reduction which is applied against a weapon's AutoPenalty value.
            Setting this value to 0 will result in the AFTHB modifiers being applied directly to a weapon's AutoPenalty value (Vanilla style).
            This multiple is applied to the AFTHB modifier, so we get a reasonable percentage value by which to alter AutoPenalty. As an example, if a weapon has AutoPenalty 7 and an attachment has AutoFireToHitBonus of 5, setting this value to 3 will result in the weapons AutoPenalty being reduced by 15% per round fired.
            If you set this value to 0, you use the Vanilla system which results in a flat -2CTH against only the first rounds penalty.

properties.name: DYNAMIC_AIMING_LIMITS
properties.description:
When set to TRUE, the number of "extra aiming levels" possible is determined by the weapon type, scope type, and whether or not a bipod is being used.
            In general, pistols allow no more than 2 extra aiming levels. Only scoped sniper rifles with a bipod in prone stance allow 8 aiming levels!
            Note: You must have set ALLOW_EXTRA_AIM_LEVELS to TRUE for this to be used.

properties.name: AIM_LEVELS_DEPEND_ON_DISTANCE
properties.description:
If set to "TRUE", the AIM Levels you can spend depends on the distance.
            If set to "FALSE", the AIM Levels you can spend does not depend on the distance (old behavior).

properties.name: AIM_LEVELS_COMPATIBILITY_OPTION
properties.description:
If set to 0, the number of aim levels will be calculated based on aimbonus attributes (default).
            If set to any other value, the calculation will use minrangeforaimbonus properties instead (compatibility option).
            In this case the following formula determines the total scope bonus that will be compared to scope thresholds:
            minrangeaimbonus (gun + attachments) * AIM_LEVELS_COMPATIBILITY_OPTION / BASE_SIGHT_RANGE
            Reasonable values include 10 and BASE_SIGHT_RANGE (13).

properties.name: VERY_HIGH_POWER_SCOPE_AIM_THRESHOLD
properties.description:
From what aiming bonus a scope is considered very high power (Sniper Scope 10x).

            This value determines to what group a scope belongs to.
            Scopes are separated in groups by the aimbonus they give per click.

            With DYNAMIC_AIMING_LIMITS on TRUE, "Very High Power" scopes will get a maximum of 8 aimclicks.
            "Very High Power" scopes will get a maximum of 8 aimclicks.
            The final amount of aimclicks also depend on the gun type and wether or not you're using a bipod.
            High power scopes and upward will suffer from a To-Hit penalty when trying to aim while in prone position.
            You don't need to change this unless you change the aiming bonus that scopes give.

properties.name: HIGH_POWER_SCOPE_AIM_THRESHOLD
properties.description:
From what aiming bonus a scope is considered high power (Battle Scope 7x).

            This value determines to what group a scope belongs to.
            Scopes are separated in groups by the aimbonus they give per click.

            With DYNAMIC_AIMING_LIMITS on TRUE, "Very High Power" scopes will get a maximum of 8 aimclicks.
            "High Power" scopes get a maxium of 7 aimclicks.
            The final amount of aimclicks also depend on the gun type and wether or not you're using a bipod.
            High power scopes and upward will suffer from a To-Hit penalty when trying to aim while in prone position.
            You don't need to change this unless you change the aiming bonus that scopes give.

properties.name: MEDIUM_POWER_SCOPE_AIM_THRESHOLD
properties.description:
From what aiming bonus a scope is considered medium power (ACOG 10x).

            This value determines to what group a scope belongs to.
            Scopes are separated in groups by the aimbonus they give per click.

            With DYNAMIC_AIMING_LIMITS on TRUE, "Very High Power" scopes will get a maximum of 8 aimclicks.
            "Medium Power" scopes get a maxium of 6 aimclicks.
            The final amount of aimclicks also depend on the gun type and wether or not you're using a bipod.
            You don't need to change this unless you change the aiming bonus that scopes give.

properties.name: AI_SNIPER_RESTRICT_TO_ELITE
properties.description:
If set to TRUE, the system will use the remaining criteria strictly for Elite soldiers.
            This will allow Elite soldiers to have more options to become snipers while all other soldiers will be restricted to using a sniper rifle.

properties.name: AI_SNIPER_MIN_RANGE
properties.description: This is the minium weapon range for a weapon to be valid as a "sniper weapon".

properties.name: AI_SNIPER_CHANCE
properties.description: This is the percent chance that a soldier without a sniper rifle will be assigned the Sniper role assuming other criteria are met.

properties.name: AI_SNIPER_CHANCE_WITH_SR
properties.description: This is the percent chance that a soldier with a sniper rifle will be assigned the Sniper role assuming other criteria are met.

properties.name: CTH_PENALTY_FOR_TARGET_MOVEMENT
properties.description: How much Change to hit (CTH) is lost when firing at a target, for each tile the target has moved so far?

properties.name: MAX_CTH_PENALTY_FOR_MOVING_TARGET
properties.description: How much Change to hit (CTH) can be lost in total due to the movement of your target?

properties.name: CHANCE_BLINDED_BY_HEADSHOT
properties.description:
This feature adds a certain chance that a critical headshot will also render the target blind for several turns. The chance is a percentage (of 100).
            Please note that the number of blindness turns is based on the damage done by the shot, at a rate of 1 turn of blindness per 10 damage points.
            0 = Disabled.
            50 = About half of all critical headshots will cause blindness.
            100 = Every critical headshot causes blindness.

properties.name: CRITICAL_LEGSHOT_CAUSES_AP_LOSS
properties.description:
When activated, any character who is hit in the legs and knocked down will lose an additional number of APs, based on how much damage was done by the attack. Use the APBPConstants.INI value called "AP_LOSS_PER_LEGSHOT_DAMAGE" to determine how many APs are lost per 1 damage point.
            Please note that leg damage is usually very low (4-8 points is common) even when it does cause knock-downs.

properties.name: CAN_JUMP_THROUGH_WINDOWS
properties.description:
When activated, your mercs can jump through open windows by pressing Shift + 'j'.
In order to jump through a window, the merc must be facing the direction of the window, the window must be open and there has to be a free tile next to the window (the landing tile).

properties.name: CAN_JUMP_THROUGH_CLOSED_WINDOWS
properties.description:
When activated, your mercs can jump through closed windows (smashing them by jumping) by pressing Shift + 'j'.
In order to jump through a window, the merc must be facing the direction of the window and there has to be a free tile next to the window (the landing tile).

properties.name: CAN_CLIMB_ON_WALLS
properties.description: When activated, your mercs can climb on walls (that have 2 floors like buildings) by pressing Shift + 'j'.

properties.name: MAX_BACKPACK_WEIGHT_TO_CLIMB
properties.description:
MAX_BACKPACK_WEIGHT_TO_CLIMB is the maximum weight a backpack can weigh and still allow you to climb with.
The sBackpackWeightModifier in items.xml can modify that number by either making it harder (positive number modifier) 
or easier (negative number modifier). If the sBackpackWeightToClimb is -1 (default) then the option is unused.

properties.name: USE_GLOBAL_BACKPACK_SETTINGS
properties.description:
If USE_GLOBAL_BACKPACK_SETTINGS is TRUE (default), it uses the same rules for all backpacks, while if FALSE checks for 
the fAllowClimbing tag in Items.xml, and if that is true you can climb with the backpack.

properties.name: BACKPACK_WEIGHT_FACTOR
properties.description:
Heavy backpacks will slow down your mercs. They will lose one AP (up to four) for n*BACKPACK_WEIGHT_FACTOR (50 = 5.0 kg). 
Mercs will also require one more AP to change their stance once their backpack+content is heavier than BACKPACK_WEIGHT_FACTOR.

properties.name: SHOW_ENEMY_WEAPON
properties.description: Show enemy weapon name in tactical

properties.name: SHOW_ENEMY_EXTENDED_INFO
properties.description: If this is set to TRUE, show enemy weapon name, armour and head items in tactical.

properties.name: INDIVIDUAL_HIDDEN_PERSON_NAMES
properties.description: When activated, you can set which person names should be hidden in Tactical in the file 'TableData\HiddenNames.xml'.

properties.name: KNOWN_NPCS_DIFFERENT_MAPCOLOUR
properties.description: Should known NPCs use a different colour (deep blue instead of white), so we can find them more easily?

properties.name: INDIVIDUAL_ENEMY_NAMES
properties.description:
Turn this on and the game uses individual enemy names (in tactical) defined in 'TableData\EnemyNames.xml'.
            If you set SOLDIER_PROFILES_ENEMY = TRUE the name in the profile takes precedence.

properties.name: INDIVIDUAL_ENEMY_RANK
properties.description: Turn this on and the game uses individual enemy ranks (in tactical) defined in 'TableData\EnemyRank.xml'.

properties.name: IMPROVED_TACTICAL_UI
properties.description: Use colored name to show soldier's status.

properties.name: INDIVIDUAL_CIVILIAN_NAMES
properties.description: Turn this on, and the game uses individual civilian group names (in tactical) defined in 'TableData\CivGroupNames.xml'.

properties.name: SOLDIER_PROFILES_ENEMY
properties.description:
Controls whether enemy soldier can use predefined profiles from TableData/Profiles.
In the xml, one can specify name/bodytype/hair/skin/traits
If selected, the game will select a newly created soldier's data from these profiles randomly.

properties.name: SOLDIER_PROFILES_MILITIA
properties.description:
Controls whether militia can use predefined profiles from TableData/Profiles.
In the xml, one can specify name/bodytype/hair/skin/traits
If selected, the game will select a newly created soldier's data from these profiles randomly.

properties.name: ALLOW_DRIVING_VEHICLES_IN_TACTICAL
properties.description: If set to TRUE, vehicles can be driven around tactical maps.

properties.name: AP_SHARED_AMONG_PASSENGERS_AND_VEHICLE_MODE
properties.description:
Deduct APs from passengers when vehicle is moving to prevent exploits (default = 3).
0 - No change.
1 - AP deducted from vehicle are also deducted from all passengers.
2 - AP deducted from vehicle are also deducted from all passengers, but adjusted to initial APs of any given passenger.
3 - AP deducted from vehicle are also deducted from all passengers, but only to the certain threshold (default).

properties.name: AP_SHARED_AMONG_PASSENGERS_AND_VEHICLE_SCALE
properties.description: If AP_SHARED_AMONG_PASSENGERS_AND_VEHICLE_MODE is set, adjust how much APs will be deducted (0 - 200).

properties.name: ENEMY_TANKS_CAN_MOVE_IN_TACTICAL
properties.description: If set to TRUE, tanks can move around in tactical.

properties.name: ALLOW_CARS_DRIVING_OVER_PEOPLE
properties.description: If set to TRUE, cars can run over people.

properties.name: ALLOW_TANKS_DRIVING_OVER_PEOPLE
properties.description: If set to TRUE, tanks can run over people.

properties.name: CARS_RAMMING_MAX_STRUCTURE_ARMOUR
properties.description:
When shift is pressed cars can ram through structures, but only those with armour lower than specified value (0-255).
0 effectively disables the feature. Default 30.
For reference: cactus - 10, wooden furniture - 20, trees - 30, sandbags - 40, stone walls - 55, reinforced concrete - 70, rock - 85, indestructible - 127.

properties.name: ENEMY_JEEP_RAMMING_MAX_STRUCTURE_ARMOUR
properties.description:
When shift is pressed jeeps can ram through structures, but only those with armour lower than specified value (0-255).
0 effectively disables the feature. Default 30.
For reference: cactus - 10, wooden furniture - 20, trees - 30, sandbags - 40, stone walls - 55, reinforced concrete - 70, rock - 85, indestructible - 127.

properties.name: TANKS_RAMMING_MAX_STRUCTURE_ARMOUR
properties.description:
When shift is pressed tanks can ram through structures, but only those with armour lower than specified value (0-255).
0 effectively disables the feature. Default 70.
For reference: cactus - 10, wooden furniture - 20, trees - 30, sandbags - 40, stone walls - 55, reinforced concrete - 70, rock - 85, indestructible - 127.

properties.name: ENEMY_TANKS_DONT_SPARE_SHELLS
properties.description: If set to TRUE, tanks can use cannon even against single mercs and in perfect health.

properties.name: ENEMY_TANKS_BLOW_OBSTACLES_UP
properties.description: If set to TRUE, tanks can ignore chance to get through and destroy enemy cover even if it probably won't hit anyone behind it.

properties.name: ENEMY_TANKS_ANY_PART_VISIBLE
properties.description: If set to TRUE, tanks can be noticed as soon as any part of them is visible.

properties.name: ENEMIES_DONT_SPARE_LAUNCHABLES
properties.description: If set to TRUE, enemies can use launchables even against single mercs and in perfect health.

properties.name: ENEMIES_BLOW_OBSTACLES_UP
properties.description: If set to TRUE, enemies can ignore chance to get through and destroy enemy cover even if it probably won't hit anyone behind it.

properties.name: CAMO_REMOVING
properties.description:
If this is set to TRUE, you can repaint one type of camouflage by using different type camo kit on self. You can also use
            rags to completely erase the camo.
            This is important for Camouflaged/Ranger traits.

properties.name: CAMO_KIT_USABLE_AREA
properties.description:
This setting defines the percentage area of a characters body that can be painted with camo kits. Usually only the face and hands 
can be painted with camo. The rest of the body has to be camouflaged by clothing and armor which are already colored.
Setting this to 0 means camo kits are useless. At 100 camo kits can paint the whole body but cloth camo is useless.
Valid values are from 0 to 100.
default is 5

properties.name: ENHANCED_CLOSE_COMBAT_SYSTEM
properties.description:
Enhanced Close Combat System

            This option generally improves many things around the game's close combat system, like:

            * HtH hit to head deal more damage but has lesser chance to hit.
            * HtH hit to legs do half damage but has much better chance to hit.
            * HtH damage on lying enemies increased.
            * HtH damage on surprising attacks(from behind, when enemy didn't seen or heard the merc) is increased.
            * Aimed HtH attack cost less APs. If you have MA or HtH trait, this is converted into "focused punch" - martial artists
            perform their spinning kick then.
            * Attributes used for HtH attacks or stealing slightly tweaked.
            * Experience recieved for certain actions in close combat tweaked to be more logiacal (gain agility for dodging etc..)
            * Stealing all items is now possible only when the enemy is knocked down. The APs you need to steal items are now
            based on number of items you want to take. The standard APs for pickup item are charged for every item you selected to
            take. If you select more items to take from the enemy than you have APs for, the rest will remain with the enemy and a
            message occures that you haven't taken all you wanted.
            * Several minor tweaks included.

properties.name: AWARD_SPECIAL_EXP_POINTS_FOR_COMPLETING_QUESTS
properties.description:
When you complete any quest in game, every (conscious) merc in the sector will be awarded by a certain amount of
            experience points. This amount is counted as 'quest difficulty' * 'the value set here'. Setting this to zero
            will disable this feature. 100 is fine. You can go up to 5000, though you should know what you are doing.

            ( List of rewarded quests: Enrico's Letter, Food from Drassen, Kill Terrorits, Holy Chalice for Kingpin, Holy Chalice
            for Yanni, Kingpins Money, Find Joey, Rescue Maria, Imprisoned in Alma, Iinterrogated (in sector by Meduna), Hicks,
            Find Madlab, Robot, Bloodcat Lair, Find Gabby, Crepitus Queen, Chopper Pilot, Escort Skyrider, Free Dynamo, Escort
            Tourists, Free Children, Leather Shop Dream, Recruit Miguel, Impress Kingpin (win 3 box fights), Kill Deidranna!!! )

properties.name: SOLDIERS_ALWAYS_WEAR_ANY_ARMOR
properties.description:
Determines if soldiers (militia, enemies) should always have a helmet, vest and leggings.
            True = enabled, they always have all three items.
            False = disabled, classic behaviour.

properties.name: IMPROVED_INTERRUPT_SYSTEM
properties.description: Use Improved Interrupt System (IIS)?

properties.name: ROBOT_NO_READYTIME
properties.description: Should the robot be exempt from paying ready costs?

properties.name: NO_ENEMY_AUTOMATIC_WEAPON_READYING
properties.description:
Disable enemies to automatically ready their weapon, when they see our mercs. However, since it may help us to notify about 
being spotted, to compensate it a marker and enemy quote is implemented.
This setting can be 0 or 1 or 2. 
0 = nothing changed, the enemies will automatically raise their weapons, when they see us, as before
1 = enemies will not do that
2 = enemies will only TURN towards our direction, and NOT raise their weapon

properties.name: ENERGY_COST_FOR_WEAPON_WEIGHT
properties.description:
Energy cost on weapon manipulation
This is made out of two parts - the weapon recoil kick impact and the effort on keeping the weapon up based due to its weight.
Weapon weight:
The calculation of the cost is non-linear, so on lightweight guns, there is nearly no energy cost, while on very heavy guns,
the effect is significant. This is mainly important when trying to shoulder rather heavy weaponry (LMGs, anti-material SNs), 
as those are more likely adviced to be fired from hip (LMGs) or on bipod. 
Strugling with the weapon weight is reduced greatly in crouching position or if holding the gun on hip rather than shoulder. 
And it is almost or totaly erased when the weapon is resting on something or you are in prone position, best with a bipod. 
The setting here represents percentual modifier to the final cost, so you can tweak it up or down as you like. 
0 = disabled
100 = default
Max is 250 (rather excessive).

properties.name: ENERGY_COST_FOR_WEAPON_RECOIL_KICK
properties.description:
Weapon recoil kick
This is a little different from struggling with weapon weight. It is about how much the gun "kicks" our shoulder (or hand).
Single shots may not prove much effect, but on autofire this may incure some nasty energy loss with certain guns. 
The formula is based on weapon impact and weight, where weight actually help us out here, since it absorbs the back force
of the recoil. Again, the cost is reduced by stance (nearly erased by bipod and/or weapon resting, greatly reduced when 
firing from hip), foregrip etc. This is mainly important if you intend to fire many long autofire bursts, when you may 
(should) consider firing from hip as a more beneficial stance for it.
The setting here represents percentual modifier to the final cost, so you can tweak it up or down as you like. 
0 = disabled
100 = default
Max is 250 (rather excessive).

properties.name: ALL_NAMED_NPCS_DECIDE_ACTION
properties.description:
If set to TRUE, enables proper realtime decision making for any named NPC (i.e. NPCs tied to a profile). As a result such 
; NPCs are not required to be in CIV_TEAM anymore.

properties.name: ACCESS_OTHER_MERC_INVENTORIES
properties.description: Allow accessing other mercs inventories. This works just like stealing, but on your teammembers, even when they are dying or unconscious

properties.name: BACKPACKWEIGHT_LOWERS_AP
properties.description:
Get an AP penalty for filled backpacks. This includes the weight of the backpack itself
1 AP penalty for each 5kg of weight up to the penalty defined by AP_MODIFIER_PACK (default = 4)
TRUE = weightbased penalty
FALSE = no penalty

properties.name: BASIC_PERCENTAGE_APS_REGISTERED
properties.description:
Basic percent amount of enemy used APs our merc percieves and is counted towards his reaction time (make it higher to get
            ; interrupts more frequent)
            INFO: Improved Interrupt System must be enabled on game-start screen.

properties.name: PERCENTAGE_APS_REGISTERED_PER_EXP_LEVEL
properties.description:
Percent added to basic percentage per soldier's experience level (BASIC_PERCENTAGE_APS_REGISTERED + PERCENTAGE_APS_REGISTERED_PER_EXP_LEVEL gives you the percent amount of APs registered,
            which is further adjusted by range to target).
            INFO: Improved Interrupt System must be enabled on game-start screen.

properties.name: BASIC_REACTION_TIME_LENGTH
properties.description:
A value controlling how often an interrupt can be triggered, lower = more interrupts (this is an amount of registered APs after which an interrupt occurs, this value is further adjusted by stats, injuries and such though).
            INFO: Improved Interrupt System must be enabled on game-start screen.

properties.name: ALLOW_COLLECTIVE_INTERRUPTS
properties.description:
Allow collective interrupts? I.e. a merc can "give" interrupt to nearby teammate if he gets an interrupt, depends on stats exp level and such.
            INFO: Improved Interrupt System must be enabled on game-start screen.

properties.name: ALLOW_INSTANT_INTERRUPTS_ON_SPOTTING
properties.description:
Should we still allow the instant interrupts on sight as in vanilla, even in IIS? (I wouldn't recommend).
            INFO: Improved Interrupt System must be enabled on game-start screen.

properties.name: REDUCED_INSTANT_DEATH
properties.description:
If a non-comatose player-controlled merc receives damage that would kill them outright, damage is instead lowered so that they only fall 
into a coma. This only works if the damage is inflicted via gun or knife, and did not cause a death animation. 
Activating this makes the game easier.

properties.name: ENEMY_JAMS
properties.description: Enable enemy gun jams?

properties.name: NEW_RANDOM
properties.description: Use new code for random number generation

sections.name: Tactical Enemy Role Settings
sections.description: These settings allow enemy soldiers to gain certain abilities that will allow them to play a number of roles and make combat harder.

properties.name: ENEMYROLES
properties.description: This allow enemy roles in general. Needs to be set to "True" for the other role settings to have an effect.

properties.name: ENEMYROLES_TURNSTOUNCOVER
properties.description: You need to see a soldier at least this number of turns to uncover his role.

properties.name: ENEMY_MEDICS
properties.description: Are enemy medics allowed?

properties.name: ENEMY_MEDICS_MEDKITDRAINFACTOR
properties.description: How much of the normal amount will enemy medics drain their med kits? (normal would be 1.0)

properties.name: ENEMY_MEDICS_SEARCHRADIUS
properties.description: A medic's search radius to look for patients.

properties.name: ENEMY_MEDICS_WOUND_MINAMOUNT
properties.description: Medics will only heal soldiers that have lost a certain amount of health. (100 = 1 Hitpoint)

properties.name: ENEMY_MEDICS_HEAL_SELF
properties.description: Allow a medic to heal himself?

properties.name: ENEMY_OFFICERS
properties.description:
Allow enemy officers?
Officers grant bonuses to the enemy team to:
- suppression resistance
- morale
- surrender strength

properties.name: ENEMY_OFFICERS_REQUIREDTEAMSIZE
properties.description: For each officer the enemy team needs to have at least this number of soldiers.

properties.name: ENEMY_OFFICERS_MAX
properties.description: Enemy teams can have no more than this number of officers.

properties.name: ENEMY_OFFICERS_SUPPRESSION_RESISTANCE_BONUS
properties.description: Suppression resistance bonus for enemy team if officer is present. This value is for lieutenants. (x2 for captains)

properties.name: ENEMY_OFFICERS_MORALE_MODIFIER
properties.description: Moral bonus for enemy team if officer is present. (0.1 = 10% bonus)

properties.name: ENEMY_OFFICERS_SURRENDERSTRENGTHBONUS
properties.description: Surrender strength bonus for enemy team if officer is present. (0.1 = 10% bonus)

properties.name: ENEMY_GENERALS
properties.description:
Allow AI officers in the campaign. There is a finite number of generals in the game. On starting a new game (or loading an old
savegame that didn't have this feature), generals are created in some enemy towns.

properties.name: ENEMY_GENERALS_NUMBER
properties.description: How many generals can there be in the campaign? This setting is only used once, when the game is initialised, so choose wisely.

properties.name: ENEMY_GENERALS_BODYGUARDS_NUMBER
properties.description: Number of bodyguards for a general. These elite troops stick close to their general, thus making it much harder to isolate them.

properties.name: ENEMY_GENERALS_STRATEGIC_DECISION_SPEEDBONUS
properties.description:
Strategic AI decision process is sped up for every general alive. This simply lowers the time period between AI decisions, 
making the game more difficult. Note that the combined reduction of all generals cannot exceed 50%. 0.05 is for 5%.

properties.name: ENEMY_GENERALS_STRATEGIC_MOVEMENT_SPEEDBONUS
properties.description:
Strategic AI decision process is sped up for every general alive. This simply lowers the time period between AI decisions, 
making the game more difficult. Note that the combined reduction of all generals cannot exceed 50%. 0.05 is for 5%.

sections.name: Individual Militia Settings
sections.description: Settings for individual militia

properties.name: INDIVIDUAL_MILITIA
properties.description:
If this feature is active, every time a militia is created by training/PMC hiring/interrogation, a small profile stores their 
- name 
- visuals 
- record of all battles they participated 
- kills and assists 
- health ratio 
- and a few other things 
Whenever a sector with militia is loaded, this data is used to recreate a militia. As a result, militia seem to be as persistent 
as your mercenaries (so it is possible to have a veteran militia which accompanied you in several battles).

properties.name: INDIVIDUAL_MILITIA_PROMOTIONPOINTS_TO_REGULAR
properties.description:
For each kill, a militia gets 2 promotion points.  
For each assist, a militia gets 1 promotion point. 
Here we define how many promotion points a militia needs to be promoted.

properties.name: INDIVIDUAL_MILITIA_PROMOTIONPOINTS_TO_ELITE
properties.description:
For each kill, a militia gets 2 promotion points.  
For each assist, a militia gets 1 promotion point. 
Here we define how many promotion points a militia needs to be promoted.

properties.name: INDIVIDUAL_MILITIA_MANAGE_HEALTH
properties.description:
If TRUE, the game remembers the health percentage of a militia the last time it was in tactical. This percentage is used the 
next time the militia is used in tactical. As a result militia will have lowered health for a while after being wounded. 
NOTE: THIS WILL MAKE THE GAME HARDER!!!

properties.name: INDIVIDUAL_MILITIA_HOURLYHEALTHPERCENTAGEGAIN
properties.description: Every hour, militia health percentage rises by this percentage to simulate healing. Values from 0.0 to 100.0.

properties.name: INDIVIDUAL_MILITIA_DOCTORHEALMODIFIER
properties.description:
Militia can be healed via 'Doctor Militia' assignment. This modifies how effective healing is. If set to 0.01, healing one percent of militia health
costs as much as healing one merc HP.
Values from 0.01 to 1.0

sections.name: Tactical Cover System Settings
sections.description: These settings change the behavior of the new Cover Display System.

properties.name: COVER_SYSTEM_STEALTH_TRAIT_VALUE
properties.description: For every level of the stealth trait, X points (to your standard stealth value + equipment) gets added.

properties.name: COVER_SYSTEM_STEALTH_EFFECTIVENESS
properties.description:
This tell how much a stealth value of 100 will decrease the sight range of an enemy (in percentage).
            50% means that at 100 stealth level you have reduced the enemies sight range by 50%.

properties.name: COVER_SYSTEM_CAMOUFLAGE_EFFECTIVENESS
properties.description: This is similar to the STEALTH_EFFECTIVENESS, 100% wood camoflague will reduce the enemies vision if you are on wooden terrain.

properties.name: COVER_SYSTEM_STANCE_EFFECTIVENESS
properties.description: How much the stance influences the view range reduction. Prone will give you 10% (default) view reduction / cover.

properties.name: COVER_SYSTEM_LBE_EFFECTIVENESS
properties.description: Dual welding the longest sniper rifles with full attachements, having a third backup sniper rifle, one combat pack and one backpack will give a 50% (default) sight penalty with the default settings.

properties.name: COVER_SYSTEM_MOVEMENT_EFFECTIVENESS
properties.description: Running around crazy will give you a penalty of up to 50% (default).

properties.name: COVER_SYSTEM_TREE_EFFECTIVENESS
properties.description:
The cover system automaticly calculates how dense an object it.
            This will tell you how much percent of vision should be decreased if the object is 100% dense, and the object is between you and the enemy of course, and is something like a tree or a rock (walls will always block full).
            If you put it to a realistic setting, where solid stuff always blocks enemy views, view ranges are too bad and on certain maps it gets hard to find people, so default is only a 50% vision decrease.

properties.name: COVER_SYSTEM_UPDATE_DELAY
properties.description:
If you let the display cover refresh via the 'END' key toggle, this is the refresh interval (in ms) used to redisplay the cover.
            The cover calculation is relativly hard on the cpu, so default are only two refreshes a second.

properties.name: COVER_SYSTEM_ADDITIONAL_TILE_PROPERTIES
properties.description:
Use xml-defined properties for various properties of tiles in your surroundings. These can modify camo, stealth, and sound
            effectiveness and the trap level of bombs you plant.

properties.name: COVER_SYSTEM_STATIC_SHADOWS_DECREASE_BRIGHTNESS
properties.description: Static shadows decrease brightness

properties.name: COVER_SYSTEM_ALTERNATE_MULTI_TERRAIN_CAMO_CALCULATION
properties.description:
Camo affinities will be used as caps not multipliers.
            It will be possible to achieve perfect camo on mixed terrain using mixed camo types.
            Works only if COVER_SYSTEM_ADDITIONAL_TILE_PROPERTIES = TRUE.

properties.name: COVER_TOOLTIP_DISPLAY_DETAILED_TILE_PROPERTIES
properties.description:
Cover tooltip ("f") will display detailed properties and their values.
            Works only if COVER_SYSTEM_ADDITIONAL_TILE_PROPERTIES = TRUE.

sections.name: Tactical Suppression Fire Settings
sections.description:
These settings activate and control the HAM Suppression Fire system. With this system activated, bullets can cause a target to lose APs even if they don't hit. Depending on your settings, they can also cause the target to become useless in a firefight, but also harder to hit!
The idea, in battle, is to suck out an enemy's APs so that he/she can't move at all during their next turn! This can also happen to your mercs, which necessitates using completely different tactics than in "vanilla" 1.13.

properties.name: SUPPRESSION_EFFECTIVENESS
properties.description:
Sets the overall power of suppression-fire. Basically determines how much AP loss is caused by suppression fire, which affects everything else as well.
            This is a percentage value.
            0 = Suppression is completely disabled.
            100 = Full effectiveness.

properties.name: SUPPRESSION_EFFECTIVENESS_PLAYER
properties.description:
This modifiers control suppression effectiveness for the player. They work together with SUPPRESSION_EFFECTIVENESS, not instead.            
0 = JA2 Default: Suppression is DISABLED.
100 = Suppression is fully activated.
Values over 200 are already excessive.

properties.name: SUPPRESSION_EFFECTIVENESS_AI
properties.description:
This modifiers control suppression effectiveness for the enemy. They work together with SUPPRESSION_EFFECTIVENESS, not instead.
0 = JA2 Default: Suppression is DISABLED.
100 = Suppression is fully activated.
Values over 200 are already excessive.

properties.name: SUPPRESSION_TOLERANCE_MAX
properties.description:
Maximum Suppression Tolerance value a character can have. Suppression Tolerance helps resist the effects of suppression.
            A high value here may allow some characters to become very resistant to suppression!
            NOTE: You'll cause problems if you set SUPPRESSION_TOLERANCE_MIN to a value greater then SUPPRESSION_TOLERANCE_MAX.

properties.name: SUPPRESSION_TOLERANCE_MIN
properties.description:
Minimum Suppression Tolerance value a character can have.
            A low value here may allow some low-level characters to get "pinned down" by just a few bullets flying their way.
            NOTE: You'll cause problems if you set SUPPRESSION_TOLERANCE_MIN to a value greater then SUPPRESSION_TOLERANCE_MAX.

properties.name: NEARBY_FRIENDLIES_AFFECT_TOLERANCE
properties.description: When set to TRUE, a character's Suppression Tolerance will affected by the condition and leadership skill of nearby friendly combatants. High-leadership and/or high-level friendlies that are close enough will increase a character's tolerance, while nearby dead friendlies will reduce tolerance.

properties.name: TILES_MOVED_PER_BONUS_TOLERANCE_POINT
properties.description:
Determines how many tiles a character must move per +1 tolerance bonus.
            0 = No tolerance bonus from movement.

properties.name: SUPPRESSION_SHOCK_INTENSITY
properties.description:
This controls how much Suppression Shock is taken when under fire.
            100 is the "normal" effect.
            Range is 0 (no suppression shock) to 65535 (65535% effect).
            200 is a LOT.

properties.name: MAX_SUPPRESSION_SHOCK
properties.description:
This is the absolute maximum number of shock points a character may have.
            (Shock negatively affects accuracy, but makes the character harder to hit)
            SUPPRESSION_SHOCK_EFFECTIVENESS must be set above 0 for this to have any effect.

properties.name: CTH_PENALTY_PER_TARGET_SHOCK
properties.description:
When a character is shooting at a SHOCKED target, he/she loses CTH proportionally to how shocked the target is.
            The formula is: CTH LOST = Target Shock Points * X, where X is the value of this setting.

properties.name: MAX_CTH_PENALTY_FOR_TARGET_SHOCK
properties.description:
The maximum possible CTH you can lose when shooting at a Shocked target.
            See also CTH_PENALTY_PER_TARGET_SHOCK.
            0 = No limit!.

properties.name: MIN_RANGE_FOR_FULL_TARGET_SHOCK_PENALTY
properties.description: Minimum range to target for full CTH penalty

properties.name: CTH_PENALTY_DIVISOR_FOR_PRONE_SHOCKED_TARGET
properties.description:
When shooting at a Prone, Shocked target, this value divides the shooter's CTH penalty.
            1 = Full penalty!
            2 = Half penalty.
            And so on.

properties.name: CTH_PENALTY_DIVISOR_FOR_CROUCHED_SHOCKED_TARGET_HEAD
properties.description:
When shooting at the HEAD of a Crouched, Shocked target, this value divides the shooter's CTH penalty.
            1 = Full penalty!
            2 = Half penalty.
            And so on.

properties.name: CTH_PENALTY_DIVISOR_FOR_CROUCHED_SHOCKED_TARGET_TORSO
properties.description:
When shooting at the TORSO of a Crouched, Shocked target, this value divides the shooter's CTH penalty.
            1 = Full penalty!
            2 = Half penalty.
            And so on.

properties.name: CTH_PENALTY_DIVISOR_FOR_CROUCHED_SHOCKED_TARGET_LEGS
properties.description:
When shooting at the LEGS of a Crouched, Shocked target, this value divides the shooter's CTH penalty.
            1 = Full penalty!
            2 = Half penalty.
            And so on.

properties.name: MAX_CTH_PENALTY_FROM_SHOCK
properties.description: A Shocked character loses some accuracy on any ranged attack (proportional to his current Shock level). This is the absolute maximum CTH you can lose from this effect.

properties.name: SHOCK_REDUCES_SIGHTRANGE
properties.description:
When activated, this feature causes "Shocked" characters to lose some or all of their sight, based on exactly how much suppression shock they've accumulated. You can set them to lose sightrange, gain tunnel vision, or both.
            At full shock, the character will be next to blind until those shock points dissipate.
            0 = Disabled.
            2 = Shocked characters lose sight-range.
            3 = Shocked characters get tunnel-vision.
            1 = Shocked characters lose sightrange AND get tunnel-vision.

properties.name: COWERING_PENALTY_TO_SUPPRESSION_TOLERANCE
properties.description:
When characters reach a certain level of Suppression Shock, they are considered "Cowering". When this happens, they become even less resistant to suppression fire!
            This value determines how many Tolerance points are lost when a character is Cowering.
            0 = Disable this effect.

properties.name: AI_SUPPRESS_MIN_MAG_SIZE
properties.description:
This tells the AI the minimum mag size of the weapon before suppression will be considered.
            Setting the magazine size to 0 will mean the AI will try to use suppression on every weapon which is the result you used to get when setting the AI Suppression flag to FALSE.

properties.name: AI_SUPPRESS_MIN_AMMO_REMAINING
properties.description: This tells the AI minimum remaining ammo the weapon must have to be valid for suppression.

properties.name: EXPLOSIVE_SUPPRESSION_EFFECTIVENESS
properties.description:
When this is set above 0, all blast-type explosives (Grenades, bombs, flashbangs, anything that has a blast effect) will cause suppression. This value controls how effective that suppression is, by percentage.
            0 = JA2 Default. No suppression from explosives.
            100 = Full Explosive Suppression.
            Note that suppression acts a little BEYOND the blast-radius!

properties.name: NOTIFY_WHEN_PINNED_DOWN
properties.description:
Suppression fire can suck out a character's APs so badly, that they start losing APs off their NEXT TURN.
            When this setting is TRUE, a message will appear whenever a character lost his entire AP supply for the next turn (usually this happens at -80 AP).
            Such a character will be unable to move or perform any action during his next turn, making it safer to approach and kill that character.
            The message displayed is "X is Pinned Down!" where X is the name of the character.

properties.name: MIN_DISTANCE_FRIENDLY_SUPPRESSION
properties.description:
Determines the maximum distance (in METERS!) at which characters are immune to suppression effects from friendly fire. Beyond this distance, they will suffer suppression normally from shots fired by their own teammates.
            30 = JA2 Default.

sections.name: Tactical Weather Settings
sections.description: These settings change the appearance and gameplay effects of various weather conditions, like Rain and Lightning storms.

properties.name: ALLOW_RAIN
properties.description:
If this is set to TRUE, it enables the chance of rainfall and lightning storms.
            If set to FALSE, rain and lightning storms will never appear in the game.

properties.name: RAIN_EVENTS_PER_DAY
properties.description: Possible number of weather events happening per day

properties.name: RAIN_CHANCE_PER_DAY
properties.description:
The chance per day (0 - 100%) for rain to occur. When a rain storm starts, it will rain in every sector on the map.
            Note that the intensity of rain is randomly decided by the program.

properties.name: RAIN_MIN_LENGTH_IN_MINUTES
properties.description: The minimum length of a rain storm, in minutes.

properties.name: RAIN_MAX_LENGTH_IN_MINUTES
properties.description: The maximum length of a rain storm, in minutes.

properties.name: MAX_RAIN_DROPS
properties.description: The maximum number of rain drops. For slow CPUs decrase this value.

properties.name: ALLOW_LIGHTNING
properties.description:
If set to TRUE, this allows a certain chance of lightning storms (Rain Intensity = 2).
            ALLOW_RAIN must be set to TRUE for this to work!

properties.name: MIN_INTERVAL_BETWEEN_LIGHTNINGS_IN_REAL_TIME_SECONDS
properties.description: This value sets the minimum interval between lightning strikes in real time seconds.

properties.name: MAX_INTERVAL_BETWEEN_LIGHTNINGS_IN_REAL_TIME_SECONDS
properties.description: This value sets the maximum interval between lightning strikes in real time seconds.

properties.name: MIN_INTERVAL_BETWEEN_LIGHTNING_AND_THUNDERCLAPS_IN_SECONDS
properties.description: This value sets the minimum interval between lightnings and thunderclaps in real time seconds.

properties.name: MAX_INTERVAL_BETWEEN_LIGHTNING_AND_THUNDERCLAPS_IN_SECONDS
properties.description: This value sets the maximum interval between lightnings and thunderclaps in real time seconds.

properties.name: DELAY_IN_SECONDS_IF_SEEN_SOMEONE_DURING_LIGHTNING_IN_TURNBASED
properties.description: When an enemy is spotted due to lightning in Turn-Based mode, this value determines the length of the pause (in seconds) that the game gives you to get an idea where that enemy is.

properties.name: CHANCE_TO_DO_LIGHTNING_BETWEEN_TURNS
properties.description:
This value sets the chance that ligntning occurs between turns in percentage.
            0 = Lightning does not occur in turn-based mode.
            100 = Lightning occurs after every turn.

properties.name: ALLOW_SANDSTORM
properties.description: Enable/Disable this weather appearing in the game.

properties.name: SANDSTORM_EVENTS_PER_DAY
properties.description: Possible number of this weather events happening per day.

properties.name: SANDSTORM_CHANCE_PER_DAY
properties.description: Chance of weather being triggered, evaluated for each of SANDSTORM_EVENTS_PER_DAY.

properties.name: SANDSTORM_MIN_LENGTH_IN_MINUTES
properties.description: Minimum length of weather event.

properties.name: SANDSTORM_MAX_LENGTH_IN_MINUTES

properties.name: ALLOW_SNOW

properties.name: SNOW_CHANCE_PER_DAY
properties.description: Chance of weather being triggered, evaluated for each of SANDSTORM_EVENTS_PER_DAY.

properties.name: SNOW_MIN_LENGTH_IN_MINUTES
properties.description: Minimum length of weather event.

properties.name: SNOW_MAX_LENGTH_IN_MINUTES
properties.description: Maximum length of weather event.

properties.name: WEAPON_RELIABILITY_REDUCTION_RAIN
properties.description: Reduction of weapon reliability, causing weapons to deteriorate faster and possibly jam more often.

properties.name: WEAPON_RELIABILITY_REDUCTION_THUNDERSTORM

sections.name: Environment Hazard Settings
sections.description: In this section you can enable various hazards to soldiers. These depend on the sector they are in.

properties.name: ALLOW_SNAKES
properties.description:
In some sectors, water sources harbour venomous snakes. These will occasionally attack anyone in that water. 
The chance of snakes being active can be set via 'snakechance' in SectorNames.xml. This chance is evaluated anew each turn. 
Soldiers have a small chance of evading an attack, this is raised if they have the survival trait or a knife.

sections.name: Tactical Weapon Overheating Settings
sections.description: These settings control the behavior of Weapon Overheating, its severity, and its display.

properties.name: OVERHEATING
properties.description: If TRUE, guns will slowly overheat, increasing the chance of malfunctions.

properties.name: OVERHEATING_DISPLAY_THERMOMETER
properties.description: If TRUE, a thermometer indicates the current temperature of a gun or barrel. It is coloured to emphasize the temperature.

properties.name: OVERHEATING_DISPLAY_JAMPERCENTAGE
properties.description: Should we display temperature/jam threshold (TRUE) or temperature/damage threshold (FALSE)?

properties.name: OVERHEATING_DISPLAY_THERMOMETER_RED_OFFSET
properties.description: Starting amount of red colour in the temperature bar.

properties.name: OVERHEATING_COOLDOWN_MODIFICATOR_LONELYBARREL
properties.description: Replacement barrels lying around all by themself cool down a bit faster by multiplying wih this value.

sections.name: Tactical Zombie Settings
sections.description: In this section you can specify how the dead will raise from their graves.

properties.name: ZOMBIE_RISE_BEHAVIOUR
properties.description:
How often is a corpse allowed to rise again as a zombie, if all conditions are met (corpse is free, has a head, there is still room for more zombies in the sector)?
            
0 - Every corpse spawns a zombie once
1 - A corpse can rise again forever. You'll have to find a way to permanently banish the undead....
2 - It is randomly decided if a corpse can rise
3 - A corpse spawns a zombie once, after that it's random

Note that, in order to rise, even the dead need a head.

properties.name: ZOMBIE_SPAWN_WAVES
properties.description: Should zombies spawn in waves, meaning that every few turns as many zombies as possible should rise (TRUE), or should every zombie rise individually (FALSE)?

properties.name: ZOMBIE_RISE_WAVE_FREQUENCY
properties.description: How often are waves of zombies created? 0 means never, 100 means whenever possible.

properties.name: ZOMBIE_CAN_CLIMB
properties.description: Can zombies climb roofs?

properties.name: ZOMBIE_CAN_JUMP_WINDOWS
properties.description: Can zombies jump through windows?

properties.name: ZOMBIE_EXPLODING_CIVS
properties.description:
Zombies made from corpses of civilians do not have a punch animation, which results in a deadlock if they try to punch.
TRUE: So instead, they blow up, dealing damage to everyone (setting TRUE)
FALSE: Another option is a 'simulated attack' without animation. However, this is pretty simple and rigged up, only a temporary solution. This may still result in deadlocks!

properties.name: ZOMBIE_DAMAGE_RESISTANCE
properties.description: Damage zombies take is reduced by this percentage. Valid values from -50 to 95.

properties.name: ZOMBIE_BREATH_DAMAGE_RESISTANCE
properties.description: Breah damage zombies take is reduced by this percentage. Valid values from -50 to 95.

properties.name: ZOMBIE_ONLY_HEADSHOTS_WORK
properties.description: Extra challenge: If TRUE, only headhots will do any damage, hits to the body or legs won't. Only applies to bullets, though.

properties.name: ZOMBIE_DIFFICULTY_LEVEL
properties.description:
Zombie difficulty level, determines hitpoints, stats and skills.
 
1 - Night of the Living Dead
2 - Dawn of the Dead
3 - Resident Evil
4 - 28 Days later

properties.name: ZOMBIE_RISE_WITH_ARMOUR
properties.description: If set to TRUE, zombies will be equipped with armour if it lay at the corpse they came from

properties.name: ZOMBIE_ONLY_HEADSHOTS_PERMANENTLY_KILL
properties.description:
If set on, a headshot or melee attack is required to permanently kill a zombie, unless his ZOMBIE_RISE_BEHAVIOUR says otherwise.
Setting ZOMBIE_RISE_BEHAVIOUR to 1 is recommended with this.

sections.name: Corpse Settings
sections.description: In this section you can specify settings for corpses.

properties.name: CORPSE_DELAY_UNTIL_ROTTING
properties.description: How many minutes it takes until a corpse begins to rot. Default 1440 (1 day), valid values from 720 (1/2 day) to 10080 (7 days)

properties.name: CORPSE_DELAY_UNTIL_DONE_ROTTING
properties.description: How many minutes it takes until a corpse vanishes. Default 4320 (3 days), valid values from 1440 (1 day) to 20160 (14 days)

sections.name: Tactical Fortification Settings
sections.description:
In this section you can specify fortification settings.
        
These settings control how you can set up/remove sandbags and concertina wire barriers.

properties.name: FORTIFICATION_ALLOW_IN_HOSTILE_SECTOR
properties.description: Can any fortification action be performed while there are enemies in the sector?

properties.name: ROOF_COLLAPSE
properties.description: Can roofs collapse when they or their supporting walls are hit?

properties.name: PRINTOUTTILESET
properties.description:
Option to turn out a structure's tileset and tileset index if we press 'f' while the mouse is over it. 
This is quite useful when adding fortification or interactive action data.

sections.name: Tactical Food Settings
sections.description:
In this section you can specify the food system
        
Your team needs water food, otherwise they'll starve...
If you mouse-over a merc's health bar, you will see two new values: Drink and Food. These represent the amount of drink and food 
your merc currently has. Note that 0 is the standard value (it represents the optimal value of sorts)
Every hour, your merc digests food, lowering his food and drink values. If these are too low, there are serious drawbacks:
 - his max morale will get lowered (when your starving, you wont get happy because you just found a good gun...)
 - his energy regeneration due to sleeping is lowered, meaning he needs more sleep
 - breath regenerates slower
 - his performance on assignments (training milita, doctoring, repairing...) is worse
 - if seriously out of water or food, there is a chance that he'll lose strength an health points. You can die from this!
   You can regain lost stat points via surgery with the new trait system. However, this requires the pateient to be well-fed again (both values above 0)

properties.description:
Your team needs water food, otherwise they'll starve...
If you mouse-over a merc's health bar, you will see two new values: Drink and Food. These represent the amount of drink and food 
your merc currently has. Note that 0 is the standard value (it represents the optimal value of sorts)
Every hour, your merc digests food, lowering his food and drink values. If these are too low, there are serious drawbacks:

- his energy regeneration due to sleeping is lowered, meaning he needs more sleep

- his performance on assignments (training milita, doctoring, repairing...) is worse
- if seriously out of water or food, there is a chance that he'll lose strength an health points. You can die from this!
  You can regain lost stat points via surgery with the new trait system. However, this requires the pateient to be well-fed again (both values above 0)

set this to TRUE to play with food.

sections.name: Disease Settings
sections.description: In this section you can specify disease settings.

properties.name: DISEASE
properties.description:
If DISEASE is TRUE, your mercs can get diseases. Diseases are specified in Disease.xml. You can get them from 
-insects in swamp and tropical sectors
-contact with other people, animals and the dead
-open wounds
-spoiled food (requires food system to be on)

properties.name: DISEASE_STRATEGIC
properties.description:
If DISEASE and DISEASE_STRATEGIC are set to TRUE, the first disease (arulcan plague) will also affect civilians, soldiers and militia.
It can break out in swamp and tropical sectors and spread as infected troops move around.
In bad cases, it can affect entire cities. Infected population will suffer just as your mercs do. If you don't act, this could be a severe threat to your campaign.
It does work on both sides though, the army can suffer just as well... especially if you give it a push ;-)

properties.name: DISEASE_WHO_SUBSCRIPTIONCOST
properties.description:
The World Health Organization has a website that contains a few helpful tips on diseases.
It also allows you to subscribe. This will cost you money every day; in return you have access to a new map mode that shows you where in Arulco the arulcan plague has broken out.
Requires DISEASE and DISEASE_STRATEGIC to be TRUE

properties.name: DISEASE_CONTAMINATES_ITEMS
properties.description:
If a merc with disease #0 consumes food, the food becomes contaminated - anybody eating from it will get the disease.
If a merc with disease #0 is hit by a blade or throwing knife, that item becomes contaminated - anybody hit with it will get the disease.

properties.name: DISEASE_SEVERE_LIMITATIONS
properties.description:
Unlocks more severe effects on some diseases. The possibilities include:
- getting additional permanent disabilities
- only one hand can be used for the duration of the disease
- damage to the legs precludes kicking, running, and drastically increases travel times
See Disease.xml for more details.

sections.name: Strategic Gamestart Settings
sections.description: These settings control the situation at the very beginning of the game. You can set some important parameters here.

properties.name: GAME_STARTING_TIME
properties.description:
This is the time when the game starts. This will always be on Day 1 + GAME_STARTING_TIME.
            The value is measured in seconds (3600 = 1 hour).
            For example, if you set GAME_STARTING_TIME to 3600, the game will start on Day 1, 01:00.

properties.name: FIRST_ARRIVAL_DELAY
properties.description:
This is the delay between the game start and the first merc arrival.
            This value is measured in seconds (3600 = 1 hour).
            For example, if you set GAME_STARTING_TIME to 3600 and FIRST_ARRIVAL_DELAY to 21600 you merc will arrive on Day 1, 07:00.

properties.name: DEFAULT_ARRIVAL_SECTOR_X
properties.description:
Determines the X location of your first arrival in Arulco. Use caution when changing this!
            Note that you may want to change the file SAMSites.XML, to enable "free airspace" over your intended landing zone. If the landing zone is not in free airspace at the start of the game, it will be automatically moved to a safe sector immediately after your first landing. You will not be able to land there again until you free the airspace above that sector.
            See also DEFAULT_ARRIVAL_SECTOR_Y.

properties.name: DEFAULT_ARRIVAL_SECTOR_Y
properties.description:
Determines the Y location of your first arrival in Arulco. Use caution when changing this!
            Note that you may want to change the file SAMSites.XML, to enable "free airspace" over your intended landing zone. If the landing zone is not in free airspace at the start of the game, it will be automatically moved to a safe sector immediately after your first landing. You will not be able to land there again until you free the airspace above that sector.
            See also DEFAULT_ARRIVAL_SECTOR_X.

sections.name: Strategic Interface Settings
sections.description: With these settings you can change the user interface in the STRATEGIC screen. These settings have little to no effect on actual gameplay - they are mostly visual aids and optimized interface settings.

properties.name: ALLOW_DESCRIPTION_BOX_FOR_ITEMS_IN_SECTOR_INVENTORY
properties.description:
If set to TRUE, this allows right-clicking items in the sector inventory window to get an item's Description Box. Stack Pop-ups are also allowed.
            For this to work properly, you may need to actually load the sector into memory (by going down to TACTICAL mode and then back up to STRATEGIC mode).

properties.name: STAT_PROGRESS_BARS_RED
properties.description:
Set the color of the "stat progress boxes" which are displayed behind your merc's attributes in the character info panel. This is done with three settings (RED/GREEN/BLUE).
            You can turn Stat Progress Bars on and off using the in-game Options Menu.

properties.name: STAT_PROGRESS_BARS_GREEN
properties.description:
Set the color of the "stat progress boxes" which are displayed behind your merc's attributes in the character info panel. This is done with three settings (RED/GREEN/BLUE).
            You can turn Stat Progress Bars on and off using the in-game Options Menu.

properties.name: STAT_PROGRESS_BARS_BLUE
properties.description:
Set the color of the "stat progress boxes" which are displayed behind your merc's attributes in the character info panel. This is done with three settings (RED/GREEN/BLUE).
            You can turn Stat Progress Bars on and off using the in-game Options Menu.

properties.name: INCLUDE_CONTRACTS_IN_PROJECTED_EXPENSES_WINDOW
properties.description:
Are merc salaries included in the new Projected Daily Expenses window?
            0 = Merc contracts are not included in your projected daily expenses.
            1 = The salaries of mercs with a fixed daily salary (Hamous, Conrad, Iggy, M.E.R.C mercs, etc.) is included in the Projected Daily Expenses display.
            2 = Include all salaries. A.I.M merc salaries are calculated based on their most recent contract.

properties.name: DISABLE_STRATEGIC_TRANSITION
properties.description: If disabled, the transition from the strategy screen will be skipped before entering tactical screen.

properties.name: EXTREME_IRON_MAN_SAVING_TIME_NOTIFICATION
properties.description:
Determine how to notify Player in Extreme Iron Man game, that it's a time to save.
0 - Open save screen.
1 - Pause the game.
2 - Do nothing (in auto-saves we trust).

properties.name: EXTREME_IRON_MAN_SAVING_HOUR
properties.description: Determine the hour in Extreme Iron Man when progress can be saved (0-23)

sections.name: Strategic Progress Settings
sections.description: In this section you can change how Game Progress is calculated, and various events and gameplay effects that are directly linked to progress.

properties.name: GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_KILLS
properties.description:
This setting controls the maximum number of Progress Points you can get by killing enemies. Press 'V' in the game to see your current progress value.
            The ratio between kills and progress points is determined by other settings (NUM_KILLS_PER_PROGRESS_POINT, for each difficulty level).
            Be sure, that the sum of GAME_PROGRESS_KILLS, GAME_PROGRESS_CONTROL, GAME_PROGRESS_INCOME, GAME_PROGRESS_VISITED has to be exactly 100, otherwise the game will set them to defaut values.

            Default Values:
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_KILLS = 25
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_CONTROL = 25
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_INCOME = 50
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_EXPLORED_SECTORS = 0

properties.name: GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_SECTOR_CONTROL
properties.description:
This setting controls the maximum number of Progress Points you can get from controlling important sectors (City / SAM). Press 'V' in the game to see your current progress value.
            The number of progress points you get per "important" sector is directly adjusted by this value. You will only get all these points if you control ALL the important sectors.
            Be sure, that the sum of GAME_PROGRESS_KILLS, GAME_PROGRESS_CONTROL, GAME_PROGRESS_INCOME, GAME_PROGRESS_VISITED has to be 100, otherwise the game will set them to defaut values.

            Default Values:
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_KILLS = 25
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_CONTROL = 25
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_INCOME = 50
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_EXPLORED_SECTORS = 0

properties.name: GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_MINE_INCOME
properties.description:
This setting controls the maximum number of Progress Points you can get from mine income. Press 'V' in the game to see your current progress value.
            The number of points you get is determined by comparing how much money you're making from mines to the MAXIMUM possible amount of money that can be made. Depleted/Abandoned mines don't count. Please remember that loyalty determines how much money a mine can make, so to get the maximum points you need 100% loyalty in all mining towns.
            Be sure, that the sum of GAME_PROGRESS_KILLS, GAME_PROGRESS_CONTROL, GAME_PROGRESS_INCOME, GAME_PROGRESS_VISITED has to be 100, otherwise the game will set them to defaut values.

            Default Values:
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_KILLS = 25
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_CONTROL = 25
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_INCOME = 50
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_EXPLORED_SECTORS = 0

properties.name: GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_EXPLORED_SECTORS
properties.description:
This setting controls the maximum number of Progress Points you can get from simply visiting map sectors. Press 'V' in the game to see your current progress value.
            The number of points you get for exploring a sector is directly adjusted by this value. You will only get all these points if you explore ALL sectors on the map (not including underground sectors).
            Note that you don't actually need to control those sectors - they simply need to be *visited* at least once.
            Be sure, that the sum of GAME_PROGRESS_KILLS, GAME_PROGRESS_CONTROL, GAME_PROGRESS_INCOME, GAME_PROGRESS_VISITED has to be 100, otherwise the game will set them to defaut values.

            Default Values:
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_KILLS = 25
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_CONTROL = 25
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_INCOME = 50
            GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS_FROM_EXPLORED_SECTORS = 0

properties.name: ALTERNATE_PROGRESS_CALCULATION
properties.description:
When activated, will calculate progress in a completely different way. Instead of adding up all points gathered from income, control, kills and exploration, the program will find out which of these four aspects has advanced the MOST, and will set your current progress level based only on that aspect. You can reach 100 progress by doing ANY of these without relying on any of the others.
            For example, you can reach 100 points by killing lots of enemies, or 100 points by exploring the entire map, or 100 points by maximizing income, or 100 points by controlling all cities - whichever comes first! The four fields will constantly be "competing" with each other to see which one's gained the most points thus far. So if you shift your strategy in mid-game, the progress dependency will automatically change to accomodate you!
            When activated, this feature disables all four "GAME_PROGRESS_MAX_POINTS" settings above.

properties.name: GAME_PROGRESS_MINIMUM
properties.description:
This is the absolute minimum Progress score you can have, EVER. This will be your starting Progress score, and will remain so until you gain enough Progress Points to surpass this value. At that point, progress will continue to increase normally. If your actual progress falls below this limit, it will instead be held at exactly this value until it can be raised again.
            You can use this setting to "skip" past the early combat where the foes have pathetic equipment.
            This value will also affect the inventory at Bobby Rays because it is based off game progress.

properties.name: GAME_PROGRESS_MODIFIER
properties.description:
Use this value to increase or decrease Game Progress by a flat amount of points. Note that this cannot decrease your progress below 0 or above 100.
            A positive value here will make enemies carry more advanced weapons earlier than they should, for the entire duration of the game. It will also increase the availability of advanced weapons from Bobby Ray's.
            A negative value here will keep enemy (and Bobby Ray) item levels lower for a longer time. However, it will PREVENT YOU FROM REACHING 100 PROGRESS POINTS (and the weapons associated with that progress level).

properties.name: GAME_PROGRESS_START_MADLAB_QUEST
properties.description:
This is the time in percentage, when the Madlab quest should start.
            Default Value: 35

properties.name: GAME_PROGRESS_MIKE_AVAILABLE
properties.description:
This is the time in percentage, when Mike is available.
            Default Value: 50

properties.name: GAME_PROGRESS_IGGY_AVAILABLE
properties.description:
This is the time in percentage, when Iggy is available.
            Default Value: 70

properties.name: GAME_PROGRESS_OFFENSIVE_STAGE_1
properties.description:
The queen decides to go on the offensive. WARNING: This will be hard!
AGGRESSIVE_STRATEGIC_AI must be true for this to have any effect.

properties.description:
