sections.name: Strategic Event Settings
sections.description: This section controls various scripted events that happen on the Strategy Map.

properties.name: TRIGGER_MASSIVE_ENEMY_COUNTERATTACK_AT_DRASSEN
properties.description:
Can queen send troops to reinforce Drassen like she says she's going to in the Meanwhile...?
If you set this to TRUE, this will be really pain in the ass at the beginning of the game ;-)

properties.name: AGGRESSIVE_STRATEGIC_AI
properties.description:
This enables massive counterattacks in all cities (currently hardcoded), just like in Drassen.
NOTE: These attacks will be huge. You have been warned.
0: no attacks
1: counterattacks on all cities possible
2: counterattacks on all cities possible + major offensives depending on game progress

properties.name: ENABLE_CREPITUS
properties.description:
This determines whether crepitus/creatures show up in SCI-FI MODE. They can never show up in realistic mode.
            This option requires a new game in order to work!

properties.name: CREPITUS_ATTACK_ALL_TOWNS
properties.description: This determines whether crepitus/creatures will attack other player-controlled town sectors, not just the originating town.

properties.name: WHICH_MINE_SHUTS_DOWN
properties.description:
This value selects which mine will deplete its ore reserves during the campaign.
            -1 = JA2 Default: The game will randomly select which mine is depleted.
            0 = No mine will be depleted!
            1 = San Mona (don't use this!!!)
            2 = Drassen
            3 = Alma (don't use this!!!)
            4 = Cambria
            5 = Chitzena
            6 = Grumm

sections.name: Strategic Gameplay Settings
sections.description: In this section you control the rules for the STRATEGIC portion of the game. Some of these settings can have a profound effect on the way the game is played.

properties.name: ALLOW_REINFORCEMENTS_ONLY_IN_CITIES
properties.description:
If this is set to TRUE, Enemy/Militia groups can only move between two CITY sectors if they want to reinforce an attack/defense.
            "ALLOW_REINFORCEMENTS" must be set to TRUE.

properties.name: MIN_DELAY_ENEMY_REINFORCEMENTS
properties.description:
Reinforcements minimum+random turn delay and minimum+random units enter after they been called.
Enemy reinforcement will arrive minimum this number of turns after they are called, if 0 then is disabled.

properties.name: RND_DELAY_ENEMY_REINFORCEMENTS
properties.description:
Reinforcements minimum+random turn delay and minimum+random units enter after they been called.
Additional random delay added to minimum when reinforcements will arrive after they are called.

properties.name: MIN_ENTER_ENEMY_REINFORCEMENTS
properties.description:
Reinforcements minimum+random turn delay and minimum+random units enter after they been called.
Minimum enemy units which will enter after above delay is over.

properties.name: RND_ENTER_ENEMY_REINFORCEMENTS
properties.description:
Reinforcements minimum+random turn delay and minimum+random units enter after they been called.
Additional random enemy units to appear after passing delay.

properties.name: MIN_DELAY_MILITIA_REINFORCEMENTS
properties.description:
Reinforcements minimum+random turn delay and minimum+random units enter after they been called.
Militia reinforcement will arrive minimum this number of turns after they are called, if 0 then is disabled.

properties.name: RND_DELAY_MILITIA_REINFORCEMENTS
properties.description:
Reinforcements minimum+random turn delay and minimum+random units enter after they been called.
Additional random delay added to minimum when reinforcements will arrive after they are called.

properties.name: MIN_ENTER_MILITIA_REINFORCEMENTS
properties.description:
Reinforcements minimum+random turn delay and minimum+random units enter after they been called.
Minimum militia units which will enter after above delay is over.

properties.name: RND_ENTER_MILITIA_REINFORCEMENTS
properties.description:
Reinforcements minimum+random turn delay and minimum+random units enter after they been called.
Additional random militia units to appear after passing delay.

properties.name: NO_REMOVE_RANDOM_SECTOR_ITEMS
properties.description: Don't allow permanent items removal for no merc in that sector

properties.name: ARMY_USES_TANKS_IN_ATTACKS
properties.description: Depending on game difficulty enemy groups created during offensives can include tanks.

properties.name: ARMY_USES_TANKS_IN_PATROLS
properties.description: Depending on game difficulty enemy patrols at game start can be randomly reinforced with.

properties.name: TANK_MINIMUM_PROGRESS
properties.description: Minimum progress required for tanks to appear.

properties.name: ARMY_USES_JEEPS_IN_ATTACKS
properties.description: Depending on game difficulty enemy groups created during offensives can include tanks.

properties.name: ARMY_USES_JEEPS_IN_PATROLS
properties.description: Depending on game difficulty enemy patrols at game start can be randomly reinforced with.

properties.name: JEEP_MINIMUM_PROGRESS
properties.description: Minimum progress required for tanks to appear.

properties.name: VEHICLE_INVENTORY
properties.description: Should vehicles have an inventory?

properties.name: HUMVEE_OFFROAD
properties.description: If enabled, this feature will allow the HUMVEE jeep to travel off roads. It cannot go everywhere, but can drive through plains, fields, hills, and light forests.

properties.name: AUTORESOLVE_LUCK_FACTOR
properties.description:
Controls the importance of luck in determining the results of auto-resolve combat. You can use fractional values here.
            1.0 = Luck is mostly irrelevant. Battles will be won based on the respective skills of the participants.
            2.0 = JA2 1.13 Default: Luck is just as important as the respective skills of the participants.

properties.name: NO_ENEMY_DETECTION_WITHOUT_RECON
properties.description:
If set to TRUE, enemy units moving through previously-explored sectors are not automatically shown on the strategy map. This allows them to sneak inside your territory even after you've explored a large portion of the map.
            Militia can detect enemies in sectors adjacent to their location, but mercs cannot. Skyrider can also detect enemies below his position, as in normal JA2.
            Also, enemies inside previously-explored cities will always appear on the map (as "?"), as in normal JA2.
            Note that some Facilities can be used to reveal enemies moving in the wilderness.

properties.name: FACILITY_EVENT_RARITY
properties.description:
Set the frequency and severity of risks triggered by using strategic facilities.
How often facility events (good or bad) occur. Increase this to make events rarer. Default = 1000.

properties.name: FACILITY_DANGER_RATE
properties.description:
Determines the amount of combined skill one needs to qualify for better results (or lesser damage) from facility events. Each event requires a different set of skills.
            0 = Facility risk results are always modified for the better, based on character skill.
            50 = Default. Characters with more than 50 combined skill will get better results, while characters with less than 50 will get worse results.
            100 = Maximum danger. Results from facility risks are usually worse than the default values in FacilityTypes.XML, and the less skills you have the more likely you are to get the worse results.
            Please note: You cannot use this to turn facility risks off. For that you need to edit the XML and remove all risks or reduce their chances to 0. This setting also doesn't guarantee good/bad results from triggering risks.

properties.name: FACTORIES
properties.description:
Facilities can produce items.
This requires defining production lines for each item in FacilityTypes.xml and some set up in SetFactoryLeftoverProgress(...)
and GetFactoryLeftoverProgress(...) in scripts/strategicmap.lua.

properties.name: ADDITIONAL_REPAIR_MODE
properties.description:
Activates the new additional repair mode.
            While the old JA 1.13 repair system goes from soldier to soldier, this algorithm goes through item types, priorizing equipped weapons/armor and highly damaged items. It starts with equipped weapons and armor, then goes to weapons/armor held in inventory and finally ends with items in backpacks.
            Thus, soldiers first repair all equipped weapons of mercs in the same sector, then all equipped armor, and so forth, always starting with the item with least durability (especially jammed guns).
            FALSE = 1.13 repair system
            TRUE = New additional repair system based on priorities

properties.name: ADVANCED_REPAIR
properties.description: TRUE: A gun can suffer permanent damage that cannot be repaired other by local smiths. To also allow this for mercs, see MERCS_CAN_DO_ADVANCED_REPAIRS in SkillSettings.ini

properties.name: ONLY_REPAIR_GUNS_AND_ARMOUR
properties.description: The only items we can repair are guns and armour.

properties.name: DIRT_GLOBAL_MODIFIER
properties.description: With this value one can increase or lower the dirt generated by all guns. Values from 0.1 to 10.0

properties.name: ALLOW_SKYRIDER_HOT_LZ
properties.description:
Set how to handle Skyrider "hot Landing Zone" options.
            0 = Don't allow Skyrider to drop off mercs in hot LZ (Vanilla style).
            1 = Allow Skyrider to drop off mercs to center of map.
            2 = Skyrider drops mercs at map edge from direction he entered the sector.
			3 = Allow Skyrider to drop your mercs as a group at a location of your choosing

properties.name: ENABLE_ALL_TERRORISTS
properties.description: Always make all the terrorists to appear in Arulco.

properties.name: ENABLE_ALL_WEAPON_CACHES
properties.description:
Enable all sectors with "secret" weapon caches. 
          (These sectors hold usually a few chests with various mediocre to good equipment.)

properties.name: MAP_ITEM_CHANCE_OVERRIDE
properties.description:
Override each map's percent likelihood of an item appearing.
Valid range = 0-100, where 0 uses the map values.
(Mainly for modders, can possibly take the fun out of the game)

properties.name: ALLOW_TAKE_PRISONERS
properties.description: Can you capture enemy soldiers?

properties.name: ENEMY_CAN_SURRENDER
properties.description:
Can you offer enemies a surrender option?
ALLOW_TAKE_PRISONERS has to be set to TRUE.

properties.name: DISPLAY_SURRENDER_VALUES
properties.description:
Display surrender values on asking for surrender. Helpful if you wonder why the enemy does not surrender at overwhelming odds.
ALLOW_TAKE_PRISONERS has to be set to TRUE.

properties.name: SURRENDER_MULTIPLIER
properties.description:
The higher this value, the more superiority you need over the enemy for them to surrender. Range: 2.0 - 10.0.
            ALLOW_TAKE_PRISONERS has to be set to TRUE.

properties.name: PLAYER_CAN_ASK_TO_SURRENDER
properties.description:
Can you offer your own surrender to the enemy? This will not work while certain quests are active, or if the enemy already asked you to surrender, and you refused.
            ALLOW_TAKE_PRISONERS has to be set to TRUE.

properties.name: PRISONER_RETURN_TO_ARMY_CHANCE
properties.description:
Chance that released soldiers join the army again.
            ALLOW_TAKE_PRISONERS has to be set to TRUE.

properties.name: PRISONER_DEFECT_CHANCE
properties.description:
Chance that interrogated soldiers decide to join your cause (they will be turned into militia of same or lower quality)
            ALLOW_TAKE_PRISONERS has to be set to TRUE.

properties.name: PRISONER_INTEL_CHANCE
properties.description: Chance that interrogated soldiers give us intel (see Intel Settings)

properties.name: PRISONER_RANSOM_CHANCE
properties.description:
Chance that interrogated soldiers pays you ransom money
            ALLOW_TAKE_PRISONERS has to be set to TRUE.

properties.name: PRISONER_INTERROGATION_POINTS_ADMIN
properties.description:
Points needed to interrogate prisoners of Admins. You can see your points on the merc's face in strategic: 145/7 means 145 points, 7 prisoners
            Interrogation first removes admin prisoners, then regulars and then elites
            If regulars and elites join your militia, there is a chance that they will be demoted, otherwise they will join as regular or veteran militia
            special prisoners do not exist... yet.

sections.name: Morale Settings
sections.description: These settings modify certain team morale aspects

properties.name: MORALE_MOD_APPEARANCE
properties.description:
Morale modifier for ugly(-2x), homely(-1x), beautiful(+1x) or 'total babe!'(+2x) people. Double if we care a lot.
Values from 0 to 5, default is 1.

properties.name: MORALE_MOD_REFINEMENT
properties.description:
Morale modifier for snob vs slob people. 1x for same and we care a lot, -1x for difference and we care, -2x for difference and we care a lot. 
Values from 0 to 5, default is 2.

properties.name: MORALE_MOD_HATEDNATIONALITY
properties.description:
Morale modifier if the other person is of a nationality we hate. Does not apply if we do not hate a nation.
Values from 0 to 5, default is 3.

properties.name: MORALE_MOD_RACISM
properties.description:
Morale modifier if the other person is not of our race and we are racist.
Values from 0 to 5, default is 3.

properties.name: MORALE_MOD_SEXISM
properties.description:
Morale modifier if the other person is of a different gender. Positive if attractive, negative if ugly. Doubled if very attractive/ugly, doubled again if we are very sexist.
Values from 0 to 5, default is 1.

properties.name: MORALE_MOD_BACKGROUND_XENOPHOBIC
properties.description:
Morale modifier if we have a xenophobic background and our background differs from theirs.

sections.name: Dynamic Opinion Settings

In this section you can specify whether mercs form dynamic opinions on each other.

sections.name: Dynamic Dialogue Settings
sections.description: In this section you can specify whether mercs talk to each other.

properties.name: DYNAMIC_DIALOGUE
properties.description:
If DYNAMIC_DIALOGUE is TRUE, mercs will comment on each other.
This can happen whenever something influences their relationship.
Mercs will accuse each other of doing something - or compliment them. Other mercs can then react and choose answers 
depending on their relations and personality.

sections.name: Item Property Settings
sections.description: These settings allow changing the properties of items and how they behave in-game. Some of these settings are simply an easier alternative to massively editing the XML files.

properties.name: EXPLOSIVES_DAMAGE_MODIFIER
properties.description:
This is a percentage-based modifier for the damage of ALL explosives. Use it if you don't want to edit the XML datafiles.
            100 = Normal damage.
            200 = Double damage.
            50 = Half damage.

properties.name: MELEE_DAMAGE_MODIFIER
properties.description:
This is a percentage-based modifier for the damage of ALL melee-weapons. Use it if you don't want to edit the XML datafiles.
            100 = Normal damage.
            200 = Double damage
            50 = Half damage.

properties.name: GUN_DAMAGE_MODIFIER
properties.description:
This is a percentage-based modifier for the damage of ALL ranged-weapons. Use it if you don't want to edit the XML datafiles.
            100 = Normal damage.
            200 = Double damage.
            50 = Half damage.

properties.name: GUN_RANGE_MODIFIER
properties.description:
This is a percentage-based modifiers for the weapon ranges. Use it if you don't want edit the XML datafiles.
            100 = Normal range.
            200 = Double range.
            50 = Half range.

properties.name: ENABLE_ARMOR_COVERAGE
properties.description:
Should the Armor Coverage value be used?
            If set to TRUE, bullets do not always strike the armor protecting the targeted bodypart - sometimes a bullet can hit in an uncovered spot, bypassing the armor completely. This is defined in the armor item's "Coverage" value.
            If set to FALSE, bullets always strike the armor protecting the targeted bodypart (if any).

properties.name: DYNAMIC_AMMO_WEIGHT
properties.description:
If set to TRUE, the weight of an ammo clip is determined by how many bullets are left in it.
            If set to FALSE, all clips of the same type will always weigh the same, regardless of how many bullets remain inside.

properties.name: AUTOFIRE_BULLETS_PER_5AP_MODIFIER
properties.description: This changes ALL automatic weapons, speeding up or slowing down their rate of fire (the "Bullets Per 5 AP" value). This allows you to have more (or less) autofire-intensive combat, without having to edit all the weapon entries in the XML file.

properties.name: STRENGTH_TO_LIFT_HALF_KILO
properties.description:
This setting tells us how many STRENGTH points we need to lift 0.5 kilograms comfortably.
            Adjust this value to make inventory weight more (or less) important for gameplay.

properties.name: MORTAR_CTH_DIVISOR
properties.description:
This is a divisor value applied to the "Chance-to-Hit" of all mortars, after all other calculations have taken place. The formula is:
            Final CTH = Original CTH divided by X, where X is the value you set here.
            Note: This is only used if Old Trait System is played

properties.name: USE_DEFAULT_SLOTS_WHEN_MISSING
properties.description:
When attachments have not been assigned for NAS, the game can add default slots that differ per item type.
            It is recommended to play with this set to FALSE when the attachments are assigned properly.
            This option is best used when playing a XML based mod that does not have the NAS xml fully updated.
            However when the mod is too different from 1.13, there will be a lot of strange and/or wrong attachments.

properties.name: ATTACHMENT_DROP_RATE
properties.description:
The chance in percentages that an attachment will have to drop with the item if an NPC dies.
            Setting this higher than 20% will unbalance your game unless you change MAX_ENEMY_ATTACHMENTS.
            Inseperable attachments will always drop. Range: 0 - 100%.

properties.name: MAX_ENEMY_ATTACHMENTS
properties.description:
The maximum amount of attachments NPC's can get on their gun when they get random equipment.
            They will usually get less attachments than this value because of randomness. Range: 2 - 30.

	  Helicopters have to be fuelled and repaired, which consumes AI resources. 
	  Enemy helicopter raids target strategically important targets to the player (towns, mines, inactive SAMs, roads, farms if

sections.name: Raid Settings
sections.description:
These settings control whether randomized raids occur in player-controlled sectors.
If the player doesn't defend his city sectors/SAM sites enough, opportunistic forces can attack them at night.
These attacks occur if these sectors have only very few mercenaries or militia present.
Raids can be done by 
- bloodcats
- zombies (requires zombie feature to be active)
- bandits
These forces will attack anyone in a sector and can also fight in autoresolve. If your forces are defeated, this will result
in a severe morale loss.

Whether a raid can happen in a sector at all is set in TableData\Maps\SectorNames.xml with the 
"bloodcatraidpossible"/"zombieraidpossible"/"banditraidpossible"-tags.

NOTE: THIS WILL MAKE THE GAME HARDER!!!

properties.description: Set to TRUE to enable Bloodcat raids.

properties.name: RAID_ZOMBIES

properties.name: RAID_BANDITS
properties.description: Set to TRUE to enable bandit raids.

base value determining how fast the forces are replenished daily. Higher means more forces.
Values from 1 to 100, default is 3.

properties.name: RAID_MAXSIZE_BLOODCATS
properties.description:
How many Bloodcats are allowed in a raid at maximum?
If the size of a bloodcat raid is lower than the defensive force' size, they will not attack.

properties.name: RAID_MAXSIZE_ZOMBIES
properties.description: How many zombies are allowed in a raid at maximum?

properties.name: RAID_MAXSIZE_BANDITS

How many bandits are allowed in a raid at maximum?
If the size of a bandit raid is lower than the defensive force' size, they will not attack.

sections.name: Militia Training Settings
sections.description: These settings control the training of Town Militia.

properties.name: MAX_MILITIA_PER_SECTOR
properties.description:
This defines the maximum size of any Militia group on the Strategic map (including Mobile groups).
            Also see "MAX_NUMBER_REBELS_IN_TACTICAL" to see how many can actually appear simultaneously in TACTICAL mode.

properties.name: NUM_MILITIA_TRAINED_PER_SESSION
properties.description:
This is the number of Militia trained in a single training session.
            If LEADERSHIP_AFFECTS_MILITIA_QUANTITY = TRUE, then this is the MAXIMUM possible number of men trained in a single session, although most mercs will train LESS than this amount.

properties.name: MIN_LOYALTY_TO_TRAIN_MILITIA
properties.description: This is the minimum loyalty a town must have before it allows you to train militia.

properties.name: MILITIA_TRAINING_RATE
properties.description: This controls how fast town militia gets trained. Increase this value to speed up Militia training.

properties.name: MILITIA_TRAINING_CARRYOVER_PROGRESS
properties.description: If set to TRUE, accumulated militia training progress is awarded to the next training session if a training session is finished.

properties.name: ALLOW_TRAINING_ELITE_MILITIA
properties.description: Allows the training of Elite militia (Dark-Blue Shirts).

properties.name: ELITE_MILITIA_TRAINING_DELAY
properties.description: The ability to train Elite Militia is delayed to this day. "ALLOW_TRAINING_ELITE_MILITIA" must be set to TRUE.

properties.name: RPC_BONUS_TO_MILITIA_TRAINING_RATE
properties.description:
The militia training bonus for RPC (as a percentage of normal training speed). RPCs (Ira, Miguel, etc) train militia a bit faster.
            0 = No bonus.
            10 = RPCs train militia 10% faster than normal.
            And so on.

properties.name: MINIMUM_LEADERSHIP_TO_TRAIN_MILITIA
properties.description:
This is the minimum leadership score a character must have to be able to train Town Militia.
            0 = no limit.

properties.name: LEADERSHIP_AFFECTS_MILITIA_QUANTITY
properties.description:
When this is activated, a militia trainer's Leadership will determine how many Town Militia are produced in each training session.
            The exact number of militia you produce depends on how far the character's leadership is above the MINIMUM_LEADERSHIP_TO_TRAIN_MILITIA value, and how far it is below the REQ_LEADERSHIP_FOR_MAX_MILITIA value.
            Characters cannot train less than 1 militia per session, and they cannot train more than the amount set in the "NUM_MILITIA_TRAINED_PER_SESSION" value.
            Only the BEST trainer in the sector determines the number of militia produced. Other trainers, if present, reduce the time it takes to train militia (as normal) but do NOT increase the number of men trained!

properties.name: REQ_LEADERSHIP_FOR_MAX_MILITIA
properties.description:
This sets the minimum Leadership a trainer must have, to be able to train a full squad of Town Militia. The size of a full squad is set in "NUM_MILITIA_TRAINED_PER_SESSION", and is normally set at 10 militia.
            Trainers with less than this much Leadership will train fewer men.
            0 = Any trainer will train a full squad.

properties.name: TEACHER_TRAIT_EFFECT_ON_LEADERSHIP
properties.description:
This value determines how much the Teacher Trait increases our "effective" leadership for the purposes of determining whether we have reached the required score to train militia. (See also MINIMUM_LEADERSHIP_TO_TRAIN_MILITIA)
            100 = no effect.
            200 = each level of "TEACHING" will double our effective leadership score. (Expert Teaching = x4!)
            Note: This is only used if Old Trait System is played

sections.name: Militia Volunteer Pool Settings
sections.description:
If MILITIA_VOLUNTEER_POOL is TRUE, we have a limited volunteer pool. If we train militia, the pool is lowered, if we run out 
	  of volunteers we cannot train militia any more. 
	  Each town sector has an assumed civilian population (see SectorNames.xml) and a loyalty value (the percentage displayed next 
	  to a town's name in the strategic map). population times loyalty equals loyal population. 
	  We can also gain volunteers by interrogating prisoners or as a result of quests.

properties.name: MILITIA_VOLUNTEER_POOL
properties.description: Toggles MILITIA_VOLUNTEER_POOL feature on and off

properties.name: MILITIA_VOLUNTEER_POOL_GAINFACTOR_HOURLY
properties.description: Volunteer gain per hour = ln(1 + loyal population * MILITIA_VOLUNTEER_POOL_GAINFACTOR_HOURLY)

properties.name: MILITIA_VOLUNTEER_POOL_GAINFACTOR_LIBERATION
properties.description: If we liberate a sector for the first time, we get loyal population times this factor volunteers instantly.

properties.name: MILITIA_VOLUNTEER_POOL_MULTIPLIER_FARM
properties.description:
Global loyal population size is increased by this factor for every farm sector we control. 
The reasoning is that controlling food supplies shows our commitment to the common people, and eases the food situation tremendously.

sections.name: Militia Strategic Movement Settings
sections.description:
If ALLOW_MILITIA_STRATEGIC_COMMAND is TRUE, we can plot paths for militia just like for merc groups or the heli.

These settings control whether we require resources to train and upgrade militia. 
	  If this feature is used, the player can convert items to get 3 resources: 
	  Guns: obtained from weapons, ammo 
	  Armour: obtained from helmets, vests, pants, LBE and face items 
	  Miscellaneous: obtained from melee weapons, launchers, grenades and bombs 
	  
	  Whenever we train or promote militia, we spend these resources: 
	  - A green militia requires 1 Gun. 
	  - A promotion from green to regular militia requires 1 Gun + 1 Armour. 
	  - A promotion from regular to elite militia requires 1 Gun + 1 Armour + 1 Misc. 
	  If we don't have enough resources, the training/promotion won't happen. 
	  Resources will be spent when we obtain militia by interrogation, but not if we recruit them from a PMC. 
	  Items can be converted into resources in the sector inventory by pressing [Alt] + [RMB], similar to how 
	  SELL_ITEMS_WITH_ALT_LMB works. 
	  Resources will be shown in the strategic map while the Militia view is active. 
	  Every time the maximum game progress increases, the resource pool is multiplied by the fraction of new and old progress. 
	  This feature requires MILITIA_USE_SECTOR_EQUIPMENT to be FALSE.

sections.name: Intel Settings
sections.description:
The player can acquire and spend the Intel resource. This resource is closely tied to espionage and information brokering.
The goal is to deepen the game experience by allowing for more espionage/intelligence/reconaissance roleplay.

Intel can be gained in several ways:
- interactive actions (like reading classified documents in a military base, hacking computers) can give one-time resources.
  see function HandleInteractiveActionResult(...) in Overhead.lua for examples (warning, spoilers!)
- interrogating prisoners can give us intel, the amount depends on prisoner type
- mercs can hide in disguise and gather intel in enemy-occupied territory. It is very strongly recommended that any mercs
  attempting to do so have the covert trait.
- You can take a camera and take photograps of important NPCs or locations of special interest. With luck, you can sell them
  on the R.I.S. website. After a few hours of verification, you will receive a intel reward.
- Recruiting some NPCs gives you tiny bits of intel.

You can spend intel in several ways:
- After you've received your first intel, you will receive an email with further tips on this. One will be the link to the 
  R.I.S. website. You can buy information on several things (troop presence and movement, enemy VIPs, location of imprisoned mercs...) here.
- Rumours say that a special trader deals high-tech weaponry exclusively for intel.

When a merc is being trained by another, we divide the bonus points given by the instructor by this value. The result is used as a bonus to the normal number of points the Student would generate on his own.

properties.name: SYNCHRONIZED_SLEEPING_HOURS_WHEN_TRAINING_TOGETHER
properties.description:
Controls whether the game tries to synchronize sleeping periods of Trainers and Trainees working together.
            0 = No sleep synchornization.
            2 = If a Trainer has gone to sleep, all of his students will immediately go to sleep.
            3 = If all Students have gone to sleep, the Trainer immediately goes to sleep.
            1 = Both options on.

properties.name: SYNCHRONIZED_WAKING_HOURS_WHEN_TRAINING_TOGETHER

            1 = Both options on.

            0 = Disabled.
            2 = If a Trainer is awake but all his students are asleep, he will rest and replenish his Stamina, until at least one Student wakes up.
            3 = If a Student is awake but his trainer is asleep, he will rest and replenish his Stamina, until his trainer wakes up. He will NOT study alone during his rest!
            1 = Both options on.
